name: Easy Pressure Cooker Pork Picadillo Rice Bowls with Lettuce & Spicy Mayo

instructions.primary_message: Wash and dry the fresh produce.
Quarter, core, and roughly chop apples. Trim, seed, and roughly chop bell peppers. Peel, halve, and roughly chop onion. Place all three in a 6-quart pressure cooker insert and set aside.

Place pork in a medium bowl and season with spices. Stir well to coat, then add to the pressure cooker along with tomatoes and water (no need to stir). Lock lid and set to pressure cook on HIGH for 10 minutes. Once done, allow the pressure to release naturally for 10 minutes, then carefully release any remaining pressure and remove the lid.
instructions.secondary_message:
680 g pork for stew
1 tbsp chili powder
1 tsp salt
½ tsp pumpkin spice mix
½ tsp black pepper
1 (411 g) can diced tomatoes

instructions.primary_message: Meanwhile, roughly chop olives. Place in a small bowl, along with raisins, and set aside.
instructions.secondary_message:
½ cup Manzanilla olives
½ cup golden raisins

instructions.primary_message: Place water and cornstarch in another small bowl. Whisk to combine the slurry and set aside.

While the pressure is releasing naturally, working one at a time, place rice pouches in the microwave, seam-side up. Heat on high for 3-4 minutes (until pouch balloons up with steam for 30 seconds). Allow steam to vent before opening pouch. (Alternatively, rice can be heated in a saucepan according to package instructions.)
instructions.secondary_message: 2 (283 g) pouch frozen Jasmine rice, pre-cooked

instructions.primary_message: Add olives, raisins, and slurry to the pressure cooker, then stir well to combine. Set to sauté on HIGH and continue to cook, stirring occasionally, until the pork picadillo is warmed through and sauce is thickened, 2-3 minutes.
Meanwhile, halve lettuce lengthwise, then slice crosswise into thin (shred-like) strips.
To serve, divide rice, pork picadillo, and lettuce between bowls. Drizzle with spicy mayo and enjoy!
